tool.name: Interactive scRNAseqApp Environment
tool.command:
# Prepare runtime configuration for the app from Galaxy parameters set -ex
# switch to the app directory inside the image so relative paths (extdata, app_config.yaml) # match where app_setup.R was installed by the Dockerfile cd /app/scRNAseqApp_project || exit 1
# Debugging: print working dir and environment to job stdout so logs show what's happening pwd ls -la echo "--- ENV ---" env echo "--- END ENV ---"
# Ensure extdata exists and copy the input dataset there (if provided) mkdir -p extdata if [ -n "$input" ]; then # use external basename; escape $ so Galaxy's templating (Cheetah) does not interpret $() as a placeholder cp "$input" extdata/"\$(basename \"$input\")" INPUT_BASENAME="\$(basename \"$input\")" else INPUT_BASENAME="" fi
# Determine which input filename to record in the config if [ -n "\$INPUT_BASENAME" ]; then INPUT_FOR_CONFIG="\$INPUT_BASENAME" else INPUT_FOR_CONFIG="$input_file" fi
# Create an app_config.yaml that app_setup.R will read by default cat > app_config.yaml <<YAML app_dir: /app/scRNAseqApp_project data_dir: /app/scRNAseqApp_project/data input_file: \${INPUT_FOR_CONFIG} title: ${title} destinationFolder: ${destinationFolder} species: ${species} doi: ${doi} locker: true YAML
# Export environment variables as well so app_setup.R can pick them up from Sys.getenv() export INPUT_FILE="\${INPUT_FOR_CONFIG}" export TITLE="${title}" export DESTINATION_FOLDER="${destinationFolder}" export SPECIES="${species}" export DOI="${doi}"
echo "Listing /app/scRNAseqApp_project:" ls -la /app/scRNAseqApp_project echo "Rscript location:" which Rscript || echo "Rscript not found" id
# Run the app setup (this should start and block while the interactive app runs) Rscript /app/scRNAseqApp_project/app_setup.R
tool.help:
Launch the interactive scRNAseq Shiny application inside a Docker container. You can supply an RDS dataset as `Input RDS dataset` and override app settings using the form fields.
The wrapper will copy the uploaded dataset to `extdata/` inside the container and create an `app_config.yaml` file from the form parameters. The R script `app_setup.R` reads that config file (or environment variables) to start the app.
